highReview.findingSummary: criteria reads state.skillTest.actionKind; no trackTestTarget in EotE, so the field is never written on the normal path; the only ability never appears in a real playerWindow.
highReview.overstatementDetail: The issue text says the real engine NEVER sets actionKind. That is false: tests.js:176 writes it when options.actionKind is passed, and tests.js:166-175 writes it when a scenario/investigator asset declares trackTestTarget (TIC 07163.js:8, 07181.js:8 do). Also tests.js:253-259 copies testTarget.actionKind into the testInitiated context (the read point 08086 uses). The conclusion is still correct for 08105/08107 because they read state.skillTest, not context.
highReview.counterEvidence: Only a different read point (context.actionKind in testInitiated) exists; 08105/08107 do not use it. No read point populates state.skillTest.actionKind for an EotE fight/investigate.

bug1.detail: assignedCards = chapter.gatherSets.flatMap(set => scope.encounterGroups.filter(...).flatMap(group => CAMPAIGN_CODES.filter(code => entryCodes.has(code) && code.startsWith('08')))). The inner flatMap ignores `group` and returns ALL 264 campaign codes for every matching encounter group. Result: every chapter's cardCodes array contains the same full 264-code set, repeated 6-10x.

bug2.detail: chapterByCode.set(code, {id,files}) is last-wins. Because every chapter lists every code, every code maps to the last chapter (theHeartOfMadnessPart2). The fallback at 302-308 then emits a scenario-ledger record pointing at that chapter's test, without checking that the file mentions the card.

dataEvidence.detail: All 8 chapters[].cardCodes sets are equal (264 unique codes each; array lengths 1848/1584/2640 because the same full list is repeated a different number of times). 6 of the 8 serialized arrays are byte-identical; 2 differ only in repetition count. The HeartPart2 chapter is the last one (line 13750 id, line 13758 cardCodes).

testRun.caveat: All green, but the tests for 08102/08105/08107 bypass the real trigger/criteria (fire() direct descriptor execution; forged skillTest.actionKind). Several approximation cards are asserted as approximations (e.g. 08113 round-end exile, 08120 cost-reduction), so green tests do not imply printed-text equivalence.

playerFindings.highConfidence: 9/9 confirmed; 0 rejected; 2 evidence-line corrections (08102 shape detail, 08130/08131 discardSelf path); 1 universal overstatement (08105/08107 'never' sets actionKind); 1 severity borderline (08083).
playerFindings.probeTraceability: The delivered _probe.mjs / _probe2.mjs do not contain any 08102/08105/08107 probe, although findings/notes claim 'real-path probe' for all three. Two delivered outputs also contradict the notes: _probe2.mjs P5 (08083) prints damage=1,horror=1 (auto-chooses the investigator, never tests the ally branch) while the notes claim horror 1->0; _probe.mjs P2 (08088) prints uses 0->0->0 (never selects the reaction) while the notes claim 0->2->2. _probe2.mjs P7 does select the reaction and prints 2->2. The conclusions are independently confirmed by this verifier's probes, but the audit's reproduction trail is unreliable.
playerFindings.referenceDrift: 08084/08085 reference line numbers are stale by 1 and 12 lines (OnTheTrail1.hs 26 vs 25; OnTheTrail3.hs 34 vs 22); the substantive claim (no elite filter) is correct.

trustAssessment.overall: Player-b's 55-card findings are largely trustworthy (all 5 requested high groups confirmed). The two acceptance ledgers are not trustworthy as evidence of behavioral equivalence: the all-card ledger's scenario fallback is structurally broken, and the player ledger's noSimplified gate does not see the approximations the entries themselves declare.

limitations: I did not re-audit all 403 cards semantically; the ledger section checks evidence traceability only.
Probes use synthetic 'probe-free-1' control entries and synthetic contexts to force windows open; they do not modify the repo and do not claim to be part of the game.
The 2 fatalMirage b-side records (08575b/08579b) are left as 'plausible, not proven' because the a-side is tested but the b-side is not literally asserted.
The full test suite was not run; only the two requested files.
The 129 scenario-ledger codes were checked against all tests/*.test.mjs for exact delimited code tokens; other evidence forms (behavior names without codes) were not accepted.
